findings.title: WmiPrvSE.exe without filesystem path — highest MRI score, already exited

peirce_chain.firstness: WmiPrvSE.exe (PID=2508) observed with parent svchost.exe (PID=656). MRI score 61.0 — highest in system. Process had already EXITED. No filesystem path recorded.
peirce_chain.secondness: WmiPrvSE.exe normally resides at C:\Windows\System32\wbem\WmiPrvSE.exe. Parent relationship is NORMAL. Missing path for exited process CAN be memory acquisition artifact. MRI 61 reflects the missing-path anomaly itself.
peirce_chain.thirdness: WMI-based lateral movement (T1047) uses WmiPrvSE.exe as execution host. Same pattern occurs with legitimate WMI queries. Single artifact insufficient to distinguish attack from administration.

findings.devil_advocate: WmiPrvSE.exe exits normally after WMI queries. Missing path is documented for exited processes in Windows 7. MRI 61 reflects the anomaly itself. SCCM/GPO could produce this pattern. Without process memory dump or persistence artifact, benign WMI cannot be excluded.
findings.corroboration: No corroborating artifact found. Single-source INFERRED.

findings.title: lsass.exe RPC connections to unknown workstation 10.3.58.4 in breach subnet

peirce_chain.firstness: lsass.exe (PID=552) has CLOSED TCP connections to 10.3.58.4:135 and :49156.
peirce_chain.secondness: lsass outbound RPC to peer IP in same /24 as confirmed Zeus. Pattern NORMAL for domain auth (NTLM/Kerberos) but also consistent with pass-the-hash. Critical unknown: is 10.3.58.4 a DC?
peirce_chain.thirdness: Without identifying 10.3.58.4 and without authentication payload, single-source with strong benign alternative.

findings.devil_advocate: lsass.exe connects via RPC for NORMAL domain auth. 10.3.58.4 may be a DC. Connections CLOSED. F-Response examiner also connected to 10.3.58.4:5681. Without identifying the host, credential relay cannot be distinguished from normal auth.
